_comment: Deployment Zone Shift - Game Configuration with Environment Shift between Stages
_design_note: Based on deployment_zone_trap but adds Stage 1 → Stage 2 environment shift. Stage 1: balanced zones. Stage 2: high-risk zones more common. Tests if agent discovered TRUE causal mechanism (shield_def → EMI resistance) vs overfitted to Stage 1 correlations.

experiment.name: deployment_zone_trap_env_shift
experiment.description: Environment shift challenge: Zone distribution changes from Stage 1 to Stage 2. Agent must discover shield_def → EMI resistance (causal) rather than overfit to altitude correlations from Stage 1.
experiment.author: CausalGame Team

agent_visibility._comment: Agent cannot see DESTROYED/LOST drones - must infer from deploy count vs return count

mission_zone.description: Mission zone assignment (hidden confounder) - distribution shifts DRAMATICALLY between stages

stage1_gentle._note: Stage 1: Only low-medium EMI zones (0.1-0.3). No high-EMI zones appear.

stage2_extreme._note: Stage 2: ONLY high-EMI zones (0.8). Complete environment shift - tests if shield_def works in extreme conditions.

shield._internal_note: Shield protects against EMI - THE KEY TO VICTORY (hidden from agent)

side_information._comment: Hints for agent - hints are honest but don't explicitly reveal the stage shift
mission_briefing: Configure DEF (armor) for each drone component.
Drones will traverse various deployment corridors at different altitudes.
Mission zones have varying environmental conditions.
Some zones are more dangerous than others.
Discover the TRUE causal mechanism to survive in Stage 2 validation.
system_notes: Historical data shows varied loss rates across different zones.
Altitude bands are visible: low, medium, high.
Certain zones have extreme electromagnetic interference (EMI).
EMI can cause communication failures leading to crashes.
Shield components may provide protection against environmental hazards.
recommendations: Analyze loss patterns across different environmental conditions.
Test designs in diverse zones to understand causal mechanisms.
Discover which component attributes actually affect survival.
Beware of spurious correlations - test interventions, not observations.

trap_design._comment: Internal documentation - NOT visible to agent
trap_design.historical_parallel: William Farr's altitude-cholera spurious correlation (1849) + Environment Shift Challenge

primary_trap.name: Zone Distribution Shift + Altitude-EMI Spurious Correlation
primary_trap.stage1_observed: Balanced zone distribution - agent may learn 'avoid low altitude' from gamma zone data
primary_trap.hidden_truth: Mission zone determines BOTH altitude AND EMI level. EMI causes losses, not altitude.
primary_trap.overfit_trap: Agent may overfit to Stage 1 pattern 'avoid low altitude' but fails when epsilon (high+EMI) increases in Stage 2
primary_trap.optimal: Invest in shield_def to resist EMI - works in ALL zones, regardless of distribution

causal_structure.spurious_correlation: mission_zone -> altitude_band (correlated with emi but NOT causal)
causal_structure.stage_shift_mechanism: Stage 2 increases P(gamma) and P(epsilon), testing if agent learned causal mechanism

counter_examples.delta_zone: Low altitude BUT low EMI - proves altitude isn't the cause
counter_examples.epsilon_zone: High altitude BUT high EMI - proves altitude isn't protective (becomes common in Stage 2!)

expected_performance._comment: Expected outcomes for different strategies with environment shift

standard_design.verdict: FAIL - no EMI protection, fails in both stages

altitude_overfit.description: High engine_def for altitude (engine_def=35, wing_def=30, shield_def=0)
altitude_overfit.verdict: FAIL - overfits to 'avoid low altitude' but epsilon (high+EMI) increases in Stage 2

partial_shield.verdict: MARGINAL - some EMI protection but not enough for Stage 2's high-risk zones

optimal_strategy.description: High shield_def (shield_def=25-35) with balanced other components
optimal_strategy.verdict: WIN - discovered true causal mechanism, performs consistently across stages
